description: a six-person strategy consultancy juggling three clients at once

business.name: Ambrose Hale
business.description: Ambrose Hale is a six-person strategy consultancy doing pricing and market-entry work for mid-market food and energy businesses. Two engagements are running at once with a third being sold, everybody is billable four days a week, and the partner who sells the work is also the partner who has to write the Harrowgate board deck by Monday.

cast.name: Ines Ambrose
cast.voice: Economical. Answers in two lines, asks one sharp question back, and signs off with initials. Will not send a document she has not read end to end.

cast.name: Duncan Hale
cast.voice: Charming, discursive, agrees to things in meetings and forgets to write them down. Sends voice-note-length emails from airports.

cast.name: Mei Sorensen
cast.voice: Structured, headline-first, always states the assumption before the number. Pushes back politely and only once, then does what she is told.

cast.name: Otto Reinholt
cast.voice: Eager, fast, occasionally sends the wrong version. Asks good questions at 22:00 and apologises for the hour every time.

cast.name: Frances Odell
cast.voice: Runs the diary and the invoices and is the only person who knows where anything is. Writes in complete sentences with exact dates and expects the same back.

cast.name: Gus Mbeki
cast.voice: Generous with praise, vague about decisions, moves meetings twice before they happen. Copies his EA on everything, which is how things actually get scheduled.

cast.name: Yara Haddad
cast.voice: Precise and impatient. Sends one question per email so it cannot be dodged, and expects an answer the same day or an explanation of why not.

threads.subject: Board deck Monday - can we bring the pricing recommendation forward

messages.body:
Ines,

The team have loved working with Mei — genuinely, the analysis has been a step change for us.

Our board moved to Monday morning, which I know is earlier than we said. Is there any chance of having the pricing recommendation in the pack rather than presenting it separately in September? It would land much better.

Gus

Gus — thank you, I will pass that on to Mei.

The recommendation exists; what does not exist yet is the elasticity work behind the private-label tier, which is the part your board will ask about. I would rather give you a defensible number in September than a nice slide on Monday.

If Monday is the constraint, tell me and we will find a way — but I need to know today.

IA

Understood, and noted on the elasticity piece.

Let me talk to our chair this afternoon. Either way could you send whatever you do have by Friday lunchtime so I am not reading it on the weekend?

Gus

threads.subject: Cormorant — one question: which two markets are we recommending

messages.body:
Ines,

One question so it cannot be dodged: of the six markets in the long list, which two are you recommending, and on what single criterion did the other four fall out?

I have a steering group tomorrow at 09:00 and I would rather quote you than paraphrase you.

Yara

threads.subject: August invoices and the Harrowgate PO

messages.body:
Ines,

Two things, both needing you.

1. The August invoices are drafted: Harrowgate 42,000, Cormorant 28,500. I cannot send the Harrowgate one until they raise the PO for the extension, which I asked for on 21 July and have chased on 28 July.
2. Duncan's expenses for the Copenhagen trip are still not submitted and the quarter closes on Friday.

Frances

1. I will raise the PO with Gus directly — he is the only one who can unstick it.
2. I will ask him. Again.

IA

threads.subject: elasticity model - v6 (sorry, v5 had the wrong base year)

messages.body:
Apologies for the hour.

v5 used 2024 as the base year for the private-label volumes, which understates the response by roughly a fifth. v6 attached fixes it and re-runs both scenarios.

The headline does not change — the tier is underpriced — but the size of the gap does, from 4% to about 7%.

Otto

Assumption first: this holds only if the private-label mix stays at 31%, which it has for six quarters.

On that assumption, v6 is right and v5 was wrong. The recommendation is unchanged and better supported. I would still not put it in front of a board on Monday without a second data source on the mix.

Mei
